title: Non-Linear Dimensionality Reduction via Diffusion Maps
text: Two Approaches: Provides dense matrix solver exact computation smaller datasets, sparse solver heavier workloads. Optimized Memory Usage: sparse implementation eliminates need allocate full N×NN \times N distance matrices. computes exact k-nearest neighbors graph fly using max-heap structure stores transition graph Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) format, reducing memory complexity 𝒪(N⋅kneighbors)\mathcal{O}(N \cdot kneighbors). rSVD solver: Eigen-decompositions matrices done via custom Randomized Singular Value Decomposition (rSVD) solver. heavy computations multithreaded use OpenMP. LAPACK finds eigenvectors small m×mm \times m matrix mm requested number dimensions. Straightforwards Design: Zero external dependencies. codebase relies strictly native R C API (including LAPACK/BLAS), OpenMP, base R stats package, ensuring straightforward compilation.

title: Non-Linear Dimensionality Reduction via Diffusion Maps
text: cDiffusion designed easy use. API consists 4 core functions: run_diffusion(): exact, dense solver. Perfect capturing global topologies small medium datasets. run_diffusion_sparse(): sparse solver. Bypasses need allocate dense N×NN \times N euclidean distance matrix taking k - nearest neighbours point converting distances Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) format. estimate_sigma(): Computes global Gaussian kernel width (σ\sigma) using Median Heuristic subsampling entry data. cdiff_kmeans(): Spectral Clustering function. applies K-means diffusion coordinates features Eigengap Heuristic automatic detection optimal number clusters.

code: library(cDiffusion)  data_matrix <- matrix(rnorm(6000), ncol = 3)  opt_sigma <- estimate_sigma(data_matrix, sample_size = 500)  model_dense <- run_diffusion(   data_matrix,    dims = 3,   sigma = opt_sigma,    n_iter = 50)  plot(model_dense$coordinates[, 1], model_dense$coordinates[, 2],     pch = 16, col = "blue",     main = "Diffusion map result",     xlab = "Diffusion Coord 1", ylab = "Diffusion Coord 2")

title: Overview of cDiffusion
text: Diffusion Maps non-linear dimensionality reduction technique. methods like PCA assume data lies flat, linear plane, Diffusion Maps designed uncover complex, folded structures (manifolds) simulating random walk (Markov chain) data points. core algorithm consists three mathematical steps: Dense Method: Calculates distances possible pairs points using single global sigma. Sparse Method: Builds k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) graph. connects point closest neighbors using adaptive, local sigma. forces algorithm “walk” strictly along shape data. Markov Normalization: affinity matrix normalized row sums. transforms matrix set transition probabilities, representing chance “jumping” one point another single step random walk. Eigendecomposition: calculate eigenvalues eigenvectors transition matrix using fast Randomized SVD (rSVD) solver. first non-trivial eigenvectors form new, reduced coordinates represent underlying geometry dataset.

what: 1. Harmonics of Diffusion Maps (The Swiss Roll)
title: Overview of cDiffusion
text: dealing continuous 1D manifold rolled 3D space (like Swiss Roll), resulting diffusion dimensions represent subsequent harmonic functions (cosine waves increasing frequencies). Plotting dimensions produces different curves (parabolas, waves, figure-eights). last dimension finally captures “width” unrolled sheet.
code: library(scatterplot3d) library(cDiffusion)  set.seed(67) N <- 7000 t <- runif(N, min = 1.5 * pi, max = 4.5 * pi) t <- sort(t)  h <- runif(N, min = 0, max = 20)  X <- t * cos(t) + rnorm(N, sd=0.3) Y <- h Z <- t * sin(t) + rnorm(N, sd=0.3) swiss_data <- cbind(X, Y, Z)  colors <- rainbow(N)  model_swiss_dense <- run_diffusion(swiss_data, dims = 5, n_iter = 100)  coords_3d <- model_swiss_dense$coordinates[, 1:5]  par(mfrow=c(1, 1), mar=c(4, 4, 4, 1))  pairs(coords_3d,        col = colors,        pch = 16,        cex = 0.4,        labels = c("Dimension 1", "Dimension 2", "Dimension 3", "Dimension 4", "Dimension 5"),       main = "First 5 Dimensions of DENSE")

title: Overview of cDiffusion
text: Toroidal Helix complex 3D shape representing coiled spring wrapped around torus. relies non-uniform sampling, extremely difficult shape traditional reduction methods. Using sparse k-NN approach, cDiffusion easily discovers underlying primary cycle manifold, unrolling complex 3D knot perfect 2D circle.
code: library(scatterplot3d) library(cDiffusion)  set.seed(67) N_points <- 5000 R <- 2    r <- 0.6   omega <- 8   u <- rbeta(N_points, 0.7, 0.7)  t <- sort(u * 2 * pi)   phi <- t theta <- omega * t  X_t <- (R + r * cos(theta)) * cos(phi) + rnorm(N_points, sd=0.03) Y_t <- (R + r * cos(theta)) * sin(phi) + rnorm(N_points, sd=0.03) Z_t <- r * sin(theta) + rnorm(N_points, sd=0.03) helix_data <- cbind(X_t, Y_t, Z_t)  helix_colors <- hsv(phi / (2*pi), 1, 1)  par(mfrow=c(1,2), mar=c(2,2,2,1)) scatterplot3d(helix_data, color = helix_colors, pch = 16, cex.symbols = 0.5,               main = "1. Toroidal Helix (3D)", angle = 60,               xlab = "X", ylab = "Y", zlab = "Z")  model_helix <- run_diffusion_sparse(helix_data, dims = 5, k_neighbors = 35, n_iter = 1000, oversampling = 20)  coords <- model_helix$coordinates   plot(coords[,1], coords[,2],       col = helix_colors, pch = 16, cex = 0.6,      main = "Diffusion Map Coordinates",       xlab = "Diff Coord 1", ylab = "Diff Coord 2")
